correctness.rationale: PASS. A finite bound-one Bessel family has PSD contraction Gram G. The finite Grothendieck/Bessel convex representation gives G=sum p_s z_s z_s* with z_s in the coordinate unit disks (real [-1,1] analog). For any v in kerG, positivity forces z_s*v=0 at every positive-weight term, so all generating vectors lie in RanG. The rank-one image of RanG intersect unit polydisk is compact and connected; it sits inside the real Hermitian operator space on this r-dimensional span (dimension r²), or symmetric real space (dimension r(r+1)/2). Fenchel–Hanner–Rådström's connected-set strengthening of Carathéodory gives at most d atoms, yielding the precise bounds. The rank-zero case is realized by one all-zero atom. This is a universal exact deductive proof, not inferred from finite sampling, and no sharpness/minimality of atom number is claimed.
residual_risks: Finite families only, probability atoms upper bounds not minimum and no infinite-family finite-support claim.
